open_drafts.title: Refresh desktop booking dates across Perth midnight
open_drafts.head: fix/desktop-perth-midnight-20261021
open_drafts.body:

Refresh editable dates every 30 seconds while idle and immediately on activation/search/picker actions. Retain valid absolute selections, remove expired dates, fall back to today only when none remain, and preserve submitted cache/live contexts and displayed/lazy result dates. No automatic search starts.

**CI qualification — unresolved lifecycle timeout:** the original code head `9ed31ad463e00637732162e0592442ae3f66668a` has a **failed Windows push execution** alongside two later successful PR checks. The first summary omitted the push run after relying on a PR-event-only helper. The report and checklist now require an all-event audit. Later passes do not clear the failure, and its cause has not been attributed to #14 or established as the earlier #13 stall.

**Dependency:** separate draft stacked on unchanged [#13](https://github.com/Jarryd22/golfhub-perth/pull/13), `8b01866f3783d9ef021e114c81c139dede1facc1`, after #9→#10→#11→#12. Canonical-source reconciliation remains pending; unavailable newer dirty desktop/mobile source is untouched.

Validation and investigation:
- **15 new midnight regressions pass**. Exact #13 baseline: **4 pass, 10 failing methods (12 assertions including subcases), 1 missing-timer error**. **120 focused local checks passed** on clean code head `9ed31ad`: 77 desktop + 43 cache, Python 3.12.14 / Qt 6.11.2. The failed child has no captured stack.
- Follow-up: **40 fixed-cohort cache-close invocations passed**, 10 each on exact #13 and #14 under Linux Qt 6.11.2 and 6.12.0. **Two full lifecycle-module runs passed 11 tests each** under Qt 6.12.0. These are repeated existing tests, not new unique regressions. Every outcome is retained; no retries, relaxed checks or discarded failures.
- The lifecycle harness is byte-identical and nine relevant methods are AST-identical. open_drafts.title: Retain desktop workers until native thread cleanup completes
open_drafts.head: fix/desktop-cache-thread-lifecycle-20261020
open_drafts.body:
The desktop can release its cache or live-worker wrappers while native thread cleanup is still running, causing a crash or GUI stall and allowing close/restart to race cleanup. Retain both wrappers until `wait(0)` succeeds, retry through one owned 10 ms timer per pipeline without blocking the GUI, then delete the QThread and continue. Closing waits for outstanding references; search entry points reject closing/replacement work.

**Dependency:** separate draft stacked on unchanged [#12](https://github.com/Jarryd22/golfhub-perth/pull/12), `93d4763451358be608bff06fd0013936af36764c`, after #9–#11. Main and existing repair branches are unchanged. A fresh audit of 13 repair/agent refs found no duplicate runtime lifecycle repair; #10's cleanup was test-only.

Validation:
- **11 new real-QThread subprocess regressions pass on Qt 6.12.0 and 6.11.1.** The identical suite on untouched #12 has **5 passes / 6 failures**: five GUI stalls during a bounded native-cleanup barrier and one live refresh accepted during close. Tests cover exact destruction counts, latest queued search, responsive timers while `isRunning()==false` but `wait(0)==false`, live success/error/cancel, rapid refresh and close guards. Sockets/browser calls are blocked.
- **105 focused checks pass on final commit:** 62 desktop + 43 cache. Compile, CRLF-aware whitespace and actionlint v1.7.12 pass. Independent implementation/evidence review found no blocker.
- The identical original asynchronous **18-journey harness passes in 3/3 fresh Qt 6.12 processes** on the final application source, with no synchronous-cache or retained-wrapper workaround. It passes again on final commit `8b01866` (1.055 seconds, zero callback errors). Includes 25 player/time combinations and 28-day lazy expansion.
- Earlier exact paired #11/#12 runs both spontaneously SIGSEGV at `cache_thread_done`; a standalone QtCore reproducer also fails under both Qt versions. The last final-commit comparison also passed on untouched #12, confirming the original crash is intermittent; no crash-rate claim is made. The deterministic six baseline failures remain separate evidence.
- Four real `QApplication.exec()` probes pass cache/live work on both Qt versions: **20 completions total**, zero callback errors. These repetitions are not additional unique regression tests.
- **Remaining limitation:** the original Qt 6.11 journey passes once, then stalls in `QTest.qWait` on its second run. Its owned process was diagnostically aborted after 25 seconds; the exact native cause remains unresolved. No retry-until-green or universal asynchronous-recovery claim. The failed run is retained in the report/backlog.
- These are offline/offscreen source checks, not installed Windows/Android, native screen-reader or device delivery tests. Existing WebEngine sandbox-helper blocks and obsolete cron assertion remain outside this focused suite. No dependencies or sandbox settings changed.

[Report, reproduction and evidence](https://github.com/Jarryd22/golfhub-perth/blob/8b01866f3783d9ef021e114c81c139dede1facc1/docs/qa/2026-10-20-thread-lifecycle/REPORT.md). Cumulative checklist/backlog updated. Head `8b01866f3783d9ef021e114c81c139dede1facc1`; tree `8cb1722439a7cbd3e4f41ee76888b13ba5482b0a`. Remote commit/tree verified and checkout clean. **CI passed**: [Windows desktop — 62 tests](https://github.com/Jarryd22/golfhub-perth/actions/runs/39347972111), [Linux cache — 43 tests + actionlint](https://github.com/Jarryd22/golfhub-perth/actions/runs/39347972091). Both logs checked out PR merge `ae4c00ad494dee5bf9f7b8aa5ccb70e081c04ae2`, whose parents are the unchanged #12 base and this exact head; its tree matches `8cb1722439a7cbd3e4f41ee76888b13ba5482b0a`. Windows CI used Python 3.12 and PySide6 6.12.0 in offscreen mode.

Draft for review only. No merge, deployment, release, production workflow dispatch, booking/hold, notification, credential/security change or canonical-source integration. The unavailable newer desktop/mobile checkout remains untouched; integration into the supported source and packaged-client validation remain separate decisions.

open_drafts.title: Keep incomplete weather forecasts unavailable instead of clear and zero
open_drafts.head: fix/cache-refresh-incomplete-weather
open_drafts.body:
The health watch observed 74 October 25 records showing Clear, 0°C high/low and zero wind in cache `d91d35deb1fefa481c1e14db8b937c58f2cb46d0` at October 10 00:37 Perth, repeated from 00:26. The core parser defaults missing/null daily values to zero. Upstream nulls are inferred from that code and the published records; no live provider response was verified.

The core now reads missing, null, short or malformed daily arrays as unavailable measurements and omits an incomplete day before deriving a condition or rounding values. It preserves complete neighboring days, including later days after an invalid row. Genuine integer/float zero remains valid. Nonfinite values, invalid dates/codes and invalid precipitation/wind values cannot turn into plausible forecasts.

An omitted day returns `None`, serializes as `weather: null`, and uses the existing unavailable display. Empty location mappings remain negative-cached, so repeated desktop/shard lookups do not request weather again. The inherited PR #6 artifact validation, timestamp preservation and fallback protection remain intact. Its shared preparation continues to reject an incomplete provider response as a whole; this repair adds per-day safety in the common core, including direct desktop lookups.

Validation:
- **96 offline cache tests passed** on Python 3.12, including 9 new regression tests with fixtures for each missing/null/short array, malformed containers, invalid middle rows, genuine zeros, checkpoint/reuse/shard loading, JSON null and fallback.
- **5 offscreen PySide6 weather UI tests passed**, including 2 new tests covering incomplete weather and genuine zeros in both layouts.
- The new 9-test regression suite produces 148 failing subcases on the unchanged PR #6 base, and passes with this fix.

- Exact-head [push CI](https://github.com/Jarryd22/golfhub-perth/actions/runs/37961369899) and [PR CI](https://github.com/Jarryd22/golfhub-perth/actions/runs/37961425699) both passed all 96 cache tests and actionlint v1.7.12. Push CI checked out `cd70fd63bad89bed73b12a60d7c5d14c30c29da6`; PR CI tested its merge into unchanged PR #6 (`fb72fa3`). The remote commit/tree match the tested local branch, and the checkout is clean. UI checks were local.

Requires [#4](https://github.com/Jarryd22/golfhub-perth/pull/4) then [#6](https://github.com/Jarryd22/golfhub-perth/pull/6); only this repair's three files appear in this PR. Drafts #3–#7 were inspected and left unchanged. Head `cd70fd63bad89bed73b12a60d7c5d14c30c29da6`; tested tree `b7eb14f21576872d524f9d40dd917212e6e74231`.

open_drafts.title: Collect rendered Wembley tee times with bounded calendar fallback
open_drafts.head: fix/cache-refresh-wembley-rendered
open_drafts.body:
Wembley returned calendar-only results whenever `publicCaptchaEnabled` was true, even when ordinary public-calendar navigation could show exact times after the site's own silent check. This adds an optional Linux browser reader for Old/Tuart 9- and 18-hole products, while retaining the current calendar when rows cannot be collected.

The collector clicks only a matching calendar availability cell, validates the rendered date/product/course/round, and exports times, spaces and rebuilt safe links. It stops at an interactive challenge, denial, login, timeout or unexpected page; it never selects booking cells, reads/replays CAPTCHA responses, or exports rendered URLs/full HTML. Partial rows carry a visible coverage notice. Collection failures cannot replace a valid current calendar with stale exact rows.

Browser work has a 45-second budget, at most two calendar loads/two availability clicks per date/round, no retries, and a stop latch for later attempts in that shard. A process-local Linux guardian and pidfd cleanup cover detached descendants on timeout/executor crash. The initial calendar HTTP read retains its separate 25-second socket timeout. Only the three shards overlapping the release window install pinned Playwright/Chromium; setup has a three-minute limit and failure retains calendar collection.

Calendar parsing now accepts short/full month headings, requires explicit full cells for the requested date, and recognizes the official empty response before the ten-day/6 am Perth release boundary. Missing/ambiguous in-window products remain unknown with PR #5's stale-data safeguards.

Validation:
- **102 offline cache tests passed**, including real Chromium with every request intercepted by fixtures, all four products, exact times/spaces, safe serialization, challenge/denial stops, wrong date/course/round rejection, and real detached-child/grandchild cleanup after timeout and executor crash.
- Modeled date coverage: Oct 8/9 exact rows across both courses and round lengths; Oct 10 both rounds and Oct 11 18-hole full; Oct 18 both rounds unreleased; release boundary/month-year rollover.
- Full desktop suite: **172 passed, 11 browser tests skipped, 1 existing cron-expectation failure**. Those browser cases ran in the 102-test suite. Untouched PR #5 baseline was 132 passed plus the same cron failure; all three new Qt display tests pass.
- CRLF-aware whitespace check and independent reviews passed. Exact head `f1e0eb01170e70eda14cbf7b9030b25de751365d` passed both [push CI](https://github.com/Jarryd22/golfhub-perth/actions/runs/37593581288) and [PR CI](https://github.com/Jarryd22/golfhub-perth/actions/runs/37593585779): 102 tests plus actionlint v1.7.12 each. PR CI tested the merge into unchanged PR #5.
- Earlier head `d20c29f` had two timeout failures in browser guard tests on push CI. Chromium startup now uses the existing overall 45-second budget; individual page navigation remains capped at 15 seconds, with the same guardian deadlines and no retries. A cold-start regression test and safe failure-stage diagnostics cover this change.

**Live limitation:** this environment's outbound proxy returns HTTP 403 before reaching Wembley (Chromium tunnel failure), including with authorized network access. No new live exact-row coverage is claimed. The earlier ordinary-browser observation of nine Old 18-hole times on Oct 8 does not establish unattended Actions reliability. Keep this draft pending a bounded read-only run of this exact collector on an authorized Linux runner with ordinary Wembley access: one available date, both rounds, only advertised products, no cache publication. Preserve challenge/denial stops and record sanitized exact-row coverage. After subsequent approval and merge, observe natural publications across Old/Tuart and both rounds before claiming production recovery.

**Dependency:** targets unchanged draft #5 at `982c243b7e2645a87ecccedef4d50c93b1ebfc16`. Drafts #3, #4 and #6 remain unchanged. Head `f1e0eb01170e70eda14cbf7b9030b25de751365d`; tested tree `af776e037b73af7f32870808f3943acfa711f4fd`.

Draft for review. No merge, deployment, production workflow dispatch, booking, credential or security-setting change was performed.

open_drafts.title: Persist bounded forecasts and respect weather rate-limit cooldown
open_drafts.head: fix/cache-refresh-weather-cooldown
open_drafts.body:
Weather preparation at 08:47 and [12:06 Perth on October 7](https://github.com/Jarryd22/golfhub-perth/actions/runs/37569804692/job/112625631292) returned 36 HTTP 429 responses and five timeouts, publishing no fresh forecasts. The quota/reset cause remains unknown.

This follow-up reuses complete, validated forecasts while their original `fetched_at` is **less than one hour old**, without fetching those locations again or renewing their source timestamps. Reused forecasts carry explicit metadata. Age is rechecked after preparation, at shard lookup and at desktop rendering; tee-time fallback cannot resurrect old weather. Updated desktop source labels cached forecasts and exposes the original fetch time, while existing unstamped desktop lookups retain their behavior.

The first **429 stops queued forecast requests and pending timeout retries** for the current preparation. At most three other requests may already be in flight with four workers. No 429 is retried. Positive delta/date `Retry-After` is honored; missing, invalid, zero or past values use a **one-hour cooldown**. Concurrent rate limits retain the latest deadline, and later runs preserve it without sliding. The existing strict TLS path, four-worker bound, PR #4 timeout-retry cap and 90-second killable process remain intact.

Forecasts and cooldown are atomically checkpointed, then restored/saved with Actions cache in the preparation job independently of tee-time publication. Surfaced restore failures skip requests and preserve saved state. Persistence is best effort: cache eviction or service loss can lose an earlier cooldown; an ordinary cache miss starts a bounded fetch. No provider quota or reset behavior is assumed.

Validation:
- **87 offline cache tests** passed locally, including 33 new state/consumer/integration tests. A real killed subprocess retained completed forecasts and its 429 checkpoint.
- **3 offscreen PySide6 widget tests** passed locally for cached wording, source age and expiry.
- actionlint **v1.7.12**, CRLF-aware whitespace checks and final independent review passed.
- Exact-head [push CI](https://github.com/Jarryd22/golfhub-perth/actions/runs/37572062474) and [PR CI](https://github.com/Jarryd22/golfhub-perth/actions/runs/37572066041) both passed all 87 cache tests and actionlint v1.7.12. Push CI checked out `e84985a713d008301cdef96db7582c420b712d61`; PR CI tested its merge with unchanged PR #4. Remote tree `654941e31d469f1e6127dc2defd27477b56f7a9d` matches the local branch; the worktree is clean. GUI checks were local.
- Combined PR #4/#5/#6 validation passed **98 offline cache tests, 3 offscreen widget tests, actionlint v1.7.12 and whitespace checks** in an isolated local integration worktree. Tested tree: `f03412aeeebac5dd28bcb96da09d63ebc777bb3b`. The fallback fixture includes the provider domain required by PR #5. The integration branch remains local; no GitHub PR was merged.

**Dependency:** this draft targets `fix/cache-refresh-weather-timeouts` and requires PR #4 (`a555582`) first. Its reviewed branch is unchanged. Head `e84985a713d008301cdef96db7582c420b712d61` adds only this follow-up. PR #3 remains separate; Wembley PR #5 is independent.

Draft for review only. No merge, deployment, release, credential/security change, production dispatch or live provider probe was performed. After approved merge, verify scheduled cache reuse, rate-limit warnings/deadlines and source age; live recovery is not yet established.

open_drafts.title: Keep missing Wembley products unknown and expire stale fallback
open_drafts.head: fix/cache-refresh-wembley-fallback
open_drafts.body:
Wembley’s October 17 18-hole cache repeatedly reused an old 07:07 “available” result after the returned public calendar contained only 9-hole products. A missing configured product now produces a structured **unknown** result that cannot be replaced with historical availability. A present product can still report its own explicit availability; a partial product list cannot establish full or unreleased status.

Other isolated Wembley lookup failures may reuse a good result for at most **30 minutes**, using the original source/stale timestamp. Republication and Perth midnight cannot renew that age; missing, malformed, timezone-free or future source times disable fallback. Current weather and the official handoff stay attached to the current attempt. Other providers and the strict fresh-provider majority remain unchanged.

Validation: all **54 offline cache tests** (including 11 new Wembley regressions), actionlint **v1.7.12**, and whitespace checks passed locally. Coverage includes expiry, repeated fallback, product mismatch, partial products and exact-sheet failures, booking-horizon distinctions, midnight rollover, unaffected providers and shard publication. Independent review found no blocker. open_drafts.title: Bound weather timeout retries within shared preparation
open_drafts.head: fix/cache-refresh-weather-timeouts
open_drafts.body:
October 7 Perth publications at 06:27, 06:37 and 06:47 each retained forecasts for only 37/41 locations, with rotating SSL handshake timeouts while tee-time coverage remained complete. Failed weather requests were immediately negative-cached, leaving no recovery attempt within the preparation run.

Shared weather preparation now retries a forecast once after a one-second pause only for a typed `TimeoutError`, directly or inside `URLError`. A thread-safe allowance caps the whole run at **four extra requests** (at most 45 forecast requests for the 41 configured coordinate locations). HTTP responses including access denials/rate limits, certificate and other SSL errors, string-only timeout messages, other connection errors, geocoding and parsing errors do not qualify.

The existing verified TLS path, 25-second socket timeout, four workers, 90-second killable process deadline, atomic checkpoints and shard negative cache remain intact. Persistent failures stay unavailable; successful retries use the returned forecast. Desktop lookups remain single-attempt. Retries share the existing deadline and may leave later locations unfinished if it expires; recovery is not guaranteed.

Validation:
- All **54 offline cache tests** passed locally on Python 3.10, including 11 new retry regressions covering concurrency, request caps, fresh-run reset, exclusions, recovery, negative caching and strict TLS on both attempts.
- actionlint **v1.7.12** passed locally (release binary checksum verified).
- Whitespace check passed with `core.whitespace=cr-at-eol`, preserving the existing Python files' CRLF endings.
- Additional legacy `test_golfhub_v3.py` check: 9 passed, 7 blocked by missing PySide6, and 1 obsolete cron assertion failed. The exact same results reproduced on untouched main `25de15b`; no unrelated test/workflow changes are included.
- Independent reviews found no blocking defect.
- Exact-head [push CI](https://github.com/Jarryd22/golfhub-perth/actions/runs/37544086462) and [PR CI](https://github.com/Jarryd22/golfhub-perth/actions/runs/37544128236) both completed successfully. Each ran all 54 cache tests and actionlint v1.7.12 on Python 3.12. Push CI checked out the exact head; PR CI tested its merge with unchanged main. Remote tree `75365b0e0b0789de18125a1bc501fd26ad9c3e40` matches the tested local tree, and the checkout is clean.

Head: `a5555824cfc5123efcfcc3ca1eae7860855f1d66`, based on main `25de15b65af6f9dcad4a4d13788fb87ab976df31`. This is independent of draft PR #3; it does not change the Quick18 repair.

open_drafts.title: Bound repeated Quick18 failures across each cache shard
open_drafts.head: fix/cache-refresh-provider-circuit
open_drafts.body:
After the delayed retries added in PR #2 were exhausted, ordinary Quick18 fetches continued contacting the same slow domains for every date and round. In [run 37191045008](https://github.com/Jarryd22/golfhub-perth/actions/runs/37191045008/job/111403127669), the Oct 20–23 refresh step took 599 seconds and retained 20 stale results. Six later snapshots each added roughly 54–55 seconds. Logs/artifacts establish 20 ordinary failures plus three failed delayed recoveries; the current two-attempt fetch path implies 46 HTTP requests, although individual requests were not logged.

This cache-only repair shares a **two-transport-failure budget per Quick18 domain per shard** across ordinary and delayed fetches. Once exhausted, later requests to that domain are skipped for the rest of the shard. Persistent recognized transport failure now costs at most four HTTP attempts per domain in the current fetch path. Successful requests neither consume nor reset the failure budget, so repeated intermittent failures are bounded too. Domain aliases are serialized; unrelated providers remain parallel. Each new shard invocation starts fresh so later runs can recover.

Skipped results remain errors for the existing strict fresh-provider majority. All date/round/course entries are retained when that gate passes. Same-date/round fallback keeps its original stale timestamp; without fallback the error remains explicit. Skip reason/time and the domain's last observed error/attempt are published separately, and a skipped fallback does not invent a new last_refresh_attempt_at. Actual subsequent fetches clear old skip markers. Actions warnings and health.provider_circuit_skips expose the deferred work.

The existing heartbeat/cron cadence, 90-second weather isolation, three-domain delayed retry cap, coverage validation and booking behavior remain intact. This limits repeated failed requests; it is not a hard wall-clock deadline on a single socket operation. After two failures, a provider that recovers mid-shard waits until a later invocation; this is the deliberate traffic/freshness tradeoff.

Validation: all **54 offline cache tests** and **actionlint v1.7.12** passed locally. Eleven new regressions exercise the real core HTTP retry path (four requests per failing domain, all eight shard snapshots), concurrent aliases, cumulative failure/success interleaving, future-run recovery, error exclusions, unchanged majority rejection and truthful stale/attempt metadata. Independent review found no blocking defect.

Exact head: `cb901e9c601fa4f001ed8110215340a25bd594ec`, based on current main `25de15b65af6f9dcad4a4d13788fb87ab976df31`. Both [push CI](https://github.com/Jarryd22/golfhub-perth/actions/runs/37193010241) and [PR CI](https://github.com/Jarryd22/golfhub-perth/actions/runs/37193051986) completed successfully on this exact head. Each ran all 54 tests and actionlint v1.7.12 successfully. The remote tree matches the tested local tree (`b11070d80ed466f3a70787f4d293569bef5a1e3e`), and the local checkout is clean.

**Draft pending review. Do not merge, deploy, enable auto-merge or trigger production workflows without further authorization.** No production workflow was manually triggered, and no credentials/security settings, Android/Windows release, booking action or notification behavior were changed. After approved merge, observe circuit warnings/skips, advancing publications and recovery on subsequent scheduled runs. Circuit-only rollback should retain PR #1 and PR #2.

repositories.readme:
# GolfHub Perth

Find public golf tee times around Perth, with North/South filters, course information, scorecards and course maps.

## Download for Windows

**[Download the latest GolfHub installer](https://github.com/Jarryd22/golfhub-perth-updates/releases/latest)**

[Release notes and all versions](https://github.com/Jarryd22/golfhub-perth-updates/releases)

Download the `.exe` from the latest release and run it on your Windows 10/11 64-bit laptop. Finish any booking and close GolfHub before installing. If you already have GolfHub, install over the existing copy.

## Future updates

GolfHub 5.1.11 and later include an **Updates** button and optional checks when the app starts. When a newer stable release is available, select **Update available**, download it, then select **Install and restart**.

No GitHub account is required. Updates are announced inside GolfHub. The application verifies a signed release record and the downloaded installer before installation.

Versions are published only after the owner explicitly requests a release. Development and testing do not publish updates automatically.

This repository contains official installers and update records. You only need the `.exe`; `update.json` is for the application's update checker.

# GolfHub Perth for Android

[Download the latest approved Android release](https://github.com/Jarryd22/golfhub-perth-android-updates/releases/latest)

This repository contains the official APK downloads, release notes and signed Android update feed. Releases are published only when approved by GolfHub's owner.

## Install

Download the APK from the latest release on an Android 7.0 or newer ARM64 phone, open it, and approve Android's installation prompt. Open GolfHub, choose your dates and courses, and find tee times. Allow notifications if you want preferred-date availability alerts.

## Update

Open GolfHub and use **Updates** to check now. The app can download verified updates automatically; Android may ask you to approve installation. Production updates preserve favourites, saved alerts and settings.

Private debug/test builds have a separate signing identity. Contact Jarryd before changing from a test build to this production APK; do not uninstall it just to force an update.

Availability checks are periodic and may be delayed. Confirm the time on the course booking website before booking. This is direct APK distribution, not a Google Play listing.

Android update feed: [android-update.json](https://github.com/Jarryd22/golfhub-perth-android-updates/releases/latest/download/android-update.json)
